criteria.reasoning: The memo says the $250 gift was posted twice: G-41817 came from PayBridge transaction pbt_7Q6M77, while G-41822 was keyed by hand, and PayBridge shows one transaction. It directs deleting the later-entered G-41822 and lists a −$250.00 effect on July.

The memo identifies “Hollis Grant” and “Check 2231 ($500.00, deposited in RDC-0710-1) returned NSF on 2026-07-16.” It says to “Keep G-41810; post a reversing adjustment of −$500.00 dated 2026-07-16 in July,” and treats the $15 returned-item fee separately.

The memo explicitly says G-41802 Ruth Ann Doyle and G-41804 Samuel Ochieng were postmarked 2026-07-01 and “stay in July as FY2027 gifts.” It makes no adjustment moving either gift to FY2026 or re-dating them to the check dates.

It says “gifts stay at gross” and specifies “No CRM entry” for the fees; it does not characterize the fee difference as an error or propose reducing gifts to net amounts.
The memo states, “PayBridge paid out $3,257.13 net” on “Card gifts ... $3,335.00 gross,” and identifies “$77.87” as the PayBridge fee. This matches the required fee total and gross/net figures.

The memo identifies the $86.40 Valley Office Supply item as “a vendor refund, not a gift” and says, “Do not enter it in the CRM; Finance codes it in the general ledger.” It is also excluded from the corrected July batch total and treated separately in the bank tie-out.

The memo ties the corrected July total to the bank and includes all three required reconciling items: PayBridge fees of $77.87, the $1,000 Lindgren check, and the $86.40 Valley Office Supply refund.
